summary: Round 4, production pass. (1) THE OVERRIDE'S THIRD CONDITION HOLDS as far as it can be checked from the tree: every executable line the round-3 verdicts quoted is present verbatim and unchanged -- `sinks -> { }` in publishSegment, `new Push(run.key(), segmentKey, run.recordCount(), run.firstOffset(), via, EMPTY, grant)` in deliver, coldMode's `asked == INLINE ? PROXY : asked`, `new SegmentDelivery(Long.MAX_VALUE, false, consumers, false)`, both Push guards, mintGrant's null-issuer guard and its UncheckedIOException wrap, AssemblingSubscriber's seven-argument rebuild, and DefaultIngest's `config.directEnabled() ? new GrantIssuer(store) : null`. The line-number shifts against the round-3 citations (452->455, 507->498, 571->574) are each accounted for by comment blocks growing or shrinking at exactly the three places round 3's minors pointed at, plus the DIRECT-arm prose trim the backlog cell describes. GrantIssuer's diff is javadoc only; the backlog diff is one cell and one new row. ⚠️ STATED AS CORROBORATION, NOT PROOF: .harness/review stores verdicts and not diffs, so the round-3 bytes are not recoverable from the tree and no gate can bind them. (2) COST: the DIRECT arm adds no ingester-side request -- its Source is `sinks -> { }` -- and the mint is hoisted above both loops in deliver, so signing is once per SEGMENT, flat in consumers and in runs rather than in shards-per-node. The K pushes a node receives carry the same grant VALUE, so the one-GET-per-(node, segment) obligation is left where M5.45c's row already states it. coldMode adds no stat and no list. With directEnabled off, coldMode returns exactly what the old unconditional PROXY returned: batchBytes = Long.MAX_VALUE fails every finite bound, wantsDirect short-circuits on !directEnabled, and the MAX/MAX-cap INLINE answer is corrected to PROXY -- so the cold path is behaviour-identical for every shipping deployment. (3) REACHABILITY: FetchPolicy answers DIRECT only under capabilities.presignedUrls() && directEnabled; GrantIssuer is constructed under the same flag at the only production SegmentServing site (DefaultIngest.java:226), and IngestConfig.defaults(String) is the only production IngestConfig, so directEnabled cannot be true in production today. That is what keeps the zero-byte push round 3 raised as r3-2, and the null-issuer IllegalStateException, out of reach; both are now stated in javadoc rather than left implied. (4) CLAIMS CHECKED AGAINST SOURCE: publish's rewritten catch comment is true -- mintGrant's UncheckedIOException is collected by the loop, so a signer outage on segment 1 does not deny 2..n, and pushLoop does increment undeliverablePushes and log a WARNING naming a segment (DefaultIngest.java:442-453). The MAX/MAX claim is true: writeHeldBytes evaluates heldBytes.length inside its own per-sink try, so every subscriber completes holding nothing. 'nothing in client, plugin or http mentions FetchMode.DIRECT' is true -- grep over those src/main trees returns nothing. SubscriptionHub is at 700 lines and M5.62, M5.59 and the new M5.65 all resolve to backlog rows. One minor: a stale row pointer in GrantIssuer, one paragraph from the one this diff corrected for the same reason.

findings.title: grantFor's javadoc still hands the coalescing wiring to M5.43, which shipped without it -- this commit is what honours the rule
findings.failure_scenario: The paragraph that STATES the rule -- 'ONE GRANT PER (NODE, SEGMENT), NEVER ONE PER RUN ... THE API DOES NOT RESIST IT: this method mints fresh every call and reuses no unexpired grant for the same key. M5.43 owns the wiring that must respect it.' -- points a reader at a row that is marked done in the backlog and that shipped only IngestConfig.directEnabled and FetchPolicyConfig.directEnabled; M5.45b's and M5.45d's own cells record the rule being handed on precisely because 'M5.43 shipped the setting without it'. The enforcement is the hoisted mint in SubscriptionHub.deliver (SubscriptionHub.java:568-570), added by this commit, and nothing in GrantIssuer points there. Concretely: M5.65 is already queued to split SubscriptionHub, and the split will move deliver. Whoever does it greps for who enforces one-grant-per-(node, segment), reads this sentence, opens M5.43's row, finds a settings change with no minting in it, and concludes the rule is still unowned -- so the hoist above both loops looks like an incidental placement rather than the only thing holding the signing rate flat in runs, and moving the mint back inside the target loop reads as a harmless tidy-up. That is the mutation round 1 measured green across the whole module and the one the class javadoc exists to prevent. It is the same defect shape as round 3's M5.45d-r3-1, one paragraph up in the same file: this diff corrected the class-level paragraph that said nothing constructs GrantIssuer, and left this one naming the wrong owner. Minor rather than major: prose only, no behaviour, and DirectServingTest.SIXTYFOURRunsOnSEPARATESubscribersCostONESigning now makes the mutation die. Rule 11 applies -- record it in the commit body rather than opening round five over a sentence.
